title: FedSkillGit: Federated Skill Evolution via Version Control
abstract: arXiv:2610.21348v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model agents can improve their capabilities by evolving reusable natural-language skills from execution experience. In real-world deployments, this experience is distributed across data owners who cannot pool their raw data, which motivates federated skill evolution. The natural first design lets each client evolve the whole skill document and upload the result for server-side aggregation. That design is poorly matched to skill evolution for three reasons. An evolved document can still carry client-specific content distilled from private traces, repeated transmission of a nearly unchanged document spends communication on knowledge that the population already holds and the contribution of a single client is buried in a document that the server cannot meaningfully attribute. translated_title: FedSkillGit：基于版本控制的联邦技能演化
translated_abstract: 大语言模型智能体可以通过从执行经验中演化出可复用的自然语言技能来提升自身能力。在现实部署中，这些经验分布在无法汇集原始数据的数据所有者之间，这促使了联邦技能演化的需求。最自然的首个设计是让每个客户端演化整个技能文档，并将结果上传以供服务器端聚合。然而该设计与技能演化并不契合，原因有三：演化后的文档仍可能携带从私有轨迹中提炼的客户端特定内容；反复传输几乎未变化的文档会在群体已掌握的知识上浪费通信开销；并且单个客户端的贡献被埋没在服务器无法进行有意义归因的文档中。我们提出了FedSkillGit，一个用提交取代全文档更新的联邦技能演化框架。每个参与的客户端提交一个……（原文摘要截断）
tldr: 提出FedSkillGit框架，以类似版本控制的提交机制取代全文档更新，从而解决联邦技能演化中隐私泄露、通信浪费和贡献无法归因三大问题。
en_tdlr: FedSkillGit replaces full-document updates with version-control-style commits to address privacy leakage, communication waste, and contribution attribution issues in federated skill evolution.
